chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl who said:

I asked him about the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'Nay, it is clear verses in the chests of those who have been given knowledge' [29:49]. He said: 'They are the Imams (peace be upon them) in particular.'

key_terms.آيَاتٌ بَيِّنَاتٌ: Clear verses/signs — manifest and unambiguous Quranic revelations
key_terms.أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ: Those given knowledge — those to whom divine knowledge has been bestowed
key_terms.خَاصَّةً: In particular/exclusively — restricting the application to the Imams alone
key_terms.صُدُور: Chests — in classical Arabic, the seat of knowledge and understanding

ai.seo_question: Who are 'those who have been given knowledge' according to Imam al-Ridha in Quran 29:49?
ai.summary: Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl asked the Imam about the Quranic verse 29:49, which states that the Quran consists of clear signs preserved in the chests of those given knowledge. The Imam clarified that 'those given knowledge' refers specifically and exclusively to the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt (peace be upon them). This hadith is a cornerstone of the Shia doctrine of the Imamate, affirming that the Imams alone possess the divinely-granted, comprehensive understanding of the Quran.
